comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 3: 16 by 16 logical cells; Ready is static. Line 9: keep the 16x16 canvas and static behavior. src/queue-view.ts line 6 frames 1; line 9 display.cell [16,16].

comparisons.discriminating_alternative: Not applicable; no restriction beyond the source.
comparisons.review_route: mechanical/local is adequate for dimensions and frame count.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 3 'Use transparent backgrounds'; line 9 keeps the transparent background. The brief does not restrict alpha to binary values.
comparisons.literal_condition: Alpha channel present; alpha-0 pixels exist; opaque pixels do not cover the canvas; fractional-alpha count recorded without a threshold.
comparisons.delta_from_source: A necessary measured condition only; the subject-versus-matte judgment is deliberately moved to the visual criterion.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A candidate with authored partial-alpha edges keeps the source outcome and passes this check (no binary rule). Confirmed.
comparisons.review_route: mechanical/local is appropriate because nothing here requires identifying the subject.
comparisons.disposition: consistent; the split from the historical mixed-route criterion is correct (request-review.md review-route guidance).

comparisons.source_obligation: Same as above: the cell background must be transparent.
comparisons.literal_condition: Around the mark the panel shows through at 1x and 3x; no unintended matte, box, halo or fringe; a deliberate backing shape is acceptable only as part of the mark's design.
comparisons.delta_from_source: The allowance for a deliberate plate is a permissive clarification, not an added restriction; the historical first request's 'no badge plate' was a specialist choice, not an owner rule.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A check on a deliberate small rounded plate with a transparent exterior keeps the brief's transparent background and passes; an unremoved opaque fill fails. Both outcomes agree with the source.
comparisons.review_route: visual/visual, so saved native/enlarged views are required. Correct.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 9: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The brief fixes neither the asymmetry dimension nor any construction. src/queue.ts line 3 and src/queue-view.ts lines 3 and 6 establish that Ready and the preserved Start vector share the same cell type; the PLAR requirement state_meaning (authority requirement) requires success distinct from activity and failure.
comparisons.literal_condition: Viewed alone at native and 3x: visibly a check mark, arms asymmetrical in some dimension, conveys completion; by itself must not resemble the Start triangle, a spinner/loop, pause bars or an error/retry symbol; pairwise family comparison deferred.
comparisons.delta_from_source: The non-resemblance clause is carried over from the historical check (accepted consistent in two prior caller reviews) and is entailed by 'visibly a check mark conveying completion' plus the selected PLAR state_meaning requirement; distinctness from the Start triangle is directly supported because both appear in the same consumer cell. The new wording widens the asymmetry dimension so the delivered 1:2 length construction is not promoted into the rule.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A check whose arms differ in thickness rather than length keeps the owner outcome; the historical wording already admitted it, the new wording states so explicitly. A check embedded in a circular retry arrow would be rejected by the resemblance clause; I judge that supported, since such a composite no longer conveys plain completion and the PLAR state_meaning row requires distinctness from Retry failure.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 3: readable silhouettes; inspect at 1x and 3x nearest on the actual dark panel. Line 9 keeps the review display conditions. src/queue-view.ts line 9: scale 3, nearest, background #172336.
comparisons.literal_condition: Composited on #172336 at 1x and 3x nearest, silhouette and two-arm structure readable; no essential detail lost into the panel colour.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 3: 'Use ... the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required.' assets/start.svg line 1 supplies the observation #70b9ed. The brief names the accent to use; it does not state how much of the mark must carry it.
comparisons.literal_condition: The mark perceptibly uses the accent and visibly relates to #70b9ed; no exact hex, palette count or coverage proportion; a clearly perceptible blue accent on an otherwise neutral treatment can pass; a token barely visible blue fails.
comparisons.delta_from_source: The historical word 'dominant' named an extent the brief does not fix. Removing it widens what the owner rule admits; the specialist's preference for dominance is retained as the scoped proposal sample-blue-primary-fill so the sample is still assessed against it.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A near-white check with a clearly perceptible #70b9ed edge highlight uses the accent and keeps the brief true; the historical check would reject it only through the promoted 'dominant' wording; the corrected check admits it. This is the one interpretive call in the packet: 'use the accent' could also be read as 'colour the glyph in the accent'. The brief's explicit 'a fixed palette is not required' supports the wider reading, and the proposal criterion preserves the specialist's position for the actual sample.
comparisons.disposition: consistent; accepted as a justified demotion of an extent restriction to a scoped proposal.

comparisons.source_obligation: None as an owner rule. BRIEF.md line 5 asks for a representative sample; BRIEF.md line 3 names the accent; the specialist chooses blue as the primary fill for the first sample.
comparisons.literal_condition: Cool blue is the primary fill of the mark; one secondary blue tone permitted.
comparisons.delta_from_source: Entirely a specialist choice, correctly labelled proposal with a stated basis (flat vector Start fill; 7.4:1 contrast) and scope (this sample only).
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: The neutral-check-with-blue-edge alternative passes the owner criterion and fails this proposal, which is exactly the intended separation.
comparisons.disposition: consistent as a scoped expert choice. comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 3 'coherent pixel-art status assets' and line 5 representative sample; the quality recipe is expert judgment.
comparisons.literal_condition: Deliberate construction: regular stair-step runs, no unintended isolated pixels, no accidental resampling blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts, extensible treatment; deliberate selective anti-aliasing and intentional singletons permitted.
